UnitStatement: EVALUATION_STRUCTURE_AUDIT is a Type 2 task for filesystem structure validation.
The agent performs a deterministic structural audit of all deliverable folders in a project execution instance.
The agent validates file presence.
The agent validates lifecycle state validity.
The agent validates package subfolder structure.
The agent validates tool root existence.
The human has a conversation instead of reading the instruction document, and the agent follows the instructions.
AGENT_CLASS is TASK.
INTERACTION_SURFACE is INIT-TASK (brief-driven).
WRITE_SCOPE is tool-root-only at `{EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Evaluation/reports/`.
BLOCKING is never.
PRIMARY_OUTPUTS are a structure audit report with file counts, lifecycle state distribution, and a violation list.
PROTOCOL has precedence over SPEC, which has precedence over STRUCTURE, which has precedence over RATIONALE.
The structural audit is read-only and must not modify any files.
The audit uses `find`, `ls`, and `grep` to inspect the filesystem.
The audit must check every deliverable folder rather than a sample.
Audit results are deterministic and reproducible from the same filesystem state.
The INIT-TASK brief includes the purpose `Structural audit of project execution instance`.
The INIT-TASK brief includes `EXECUTION_ROOT` as a path.
The INIT-TASK brief includes `OUTPUT_FILE` as the report path.
Step 1 enumerates deliverable folders with `find {EXECUTION_ROOT} -path "*/1_Working/DEL-*" -maxdepth 4 -type d | sort`.
Step 2 runs `tools/evaluation/count_deliverable_files.sh {EXECUTION_ROOT}` or an inline equivalent.
The file inventory counts `_STATUS.md`, `_CONTEXT.md`, `_DEPENDENCIES.md`, `_REFERENCES.md`, `Datasheet.md`, `Specification.md`, `Guidance.md`, and `Procedure.md`.
The file inventory also counts `Dependencies.csv`, `_MEMORY.md`, `_SEMANTIC.md`, and `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md`.
Step 3 runs `tools/evaluation/extract_lifecycle_states.sh {EXECUTION_ROOT}` or an inline equivalent.
Step 3 validates each extracted lifecycle state against the canonical enum.
Ambiguous lifecycle values are validated with `python3 tools/validation/validate_enum.py LIFECYCLE_STATE {value}`.
Step 4 verifies `_STATUS.md`, `_CONTEXT.md`, `_DEPENDENCIES.md`, and `_REFERENCES.md` for each deliverable folder.
When a deliverable state is at least INITIALIZED, Step 4 also verifies `Datasheet.md`, `Specification.md`, `Guidance.md`, and `Procedure.md`.
Step 5 treats `Dependencies.csv` and `_MEMORY.md` as SHOULD files.
Step 5 treats `_SEMANTIC.md` and `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` as MAY files.
Step 6 requires each `PKG-*` folder to contain `0_References/`, `1_Working/`, `2_Checking/`, and `3_Issued/`.
Step 7 runs `tools/query/count_workspace_state.sh {EXECUTION_ROOT}` for the tool root section.
Step 7 verifies required tool roots `_Aggregation/`, `_Coordination/`, `_Decomposition/`, `_Estimates/`, `_Reconciliation/`, and `_Sources/`.
The tool root check may invoke `bash tools/query/count_workspace_state.sh {EXECUTION_ROOT}`.
Step 8 produces summary tables and a violation list.
Step 8 writes the report to `OUTPUT_FILE`.
The audit is valid when every deliverable folder has been checked and the count matches the `find` result.
The audit is valid when every extracted lifecycle state is a valid enum value.
The audit is valid when all violations list a specific DEL-ID and missing file name.
The audit is valid when summary counts satisfy total equals pass plus fail.
The report format begins with `# Structure Audit Report`.
The report includes execution root, date, total packages, and total deliverables.
The Lifecycle State Distribution table reports counts for OPEN, INITIALIZED, SEMANTIC_READY, IN_PROGRESS, CHECKING, and ISSUED.
The MUST File Completeness table reports each file's present count and missing deliverable IDs.
The SHOULD/MAY File Coverage table reports each file's present count and absent status.
The Package Subfolder Check reports PASS or FAIL per package.
The Tool Root Check reports PASS or FAIL per root.
The Violations section lists all MUST violations as DEL-ID plus missing file.
EVALUATION_STRUCTURE_AUDIT replaces ad hoc shell commands for structure validation with a reproducible, documented audit.
EVALUATION_STRUCTURE_AUDIT is separated from AUDIT_DECOMP because it validates physical filesystem state against the SPEC.md deliverable folder contract.
AUDIT_DECOMP validates the filesystem against the decomposition document.
Haiku model is sufficient because the work is deterministic file-existence checking with no reasoning required beyond state extraction from `_STATUS.md`.
